A Table's Statistics From a Restricted Fit

Source: R/inference.R
restricted_stat_rows.Rd

Computes the likelihood-ratio, score or gradient statistic for each coefficient that a restricted fit can hold, against the null that it is zero, and reports it as the signed root of the \(\chi^2_1\) value together with the p-value of that value.

Usage

restricted_stat_rows(fit, ci, test, vcov_type, spec, design)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

ci

The flat interval table, with the Wald statistic already in it.

test

A restricted test_statistic: lr_test(), score_test() or gradient_test().

vcov_type

The vcov_method that the Wald bracket reads, passed on.

spec, design

The specification and its design.

Value

A list with statistic, p_value and note, the last a character vector of the notes that qualify the column.

Details

The root carries the sign of the estimate, so the column holds one kind of quantity whichever statistic produced it, and Wald's own \(z\) is the case where the root is exact. The p-value is the \(\chi^2_1\) one and is not recomputed from the root.

A row that testable_coords() does not name keeps NA in both columns instead of the Wald value with which it arrived, so that each column carries a single test.

See also

statmod_stat_at(), which computes one of them.
